sources.title: Aki Vehtari, Andrew Gelman, Daniel Simpson, Bob Carpenter, and Paul-Christian Bürkner, Rank-normalization, folding, and localization: An improved R-hat for assessing convergence of MCMC
sources.locator: Full 26-page v5 PDF. §§1.1–2 (finite-run limitations and empirical thresholds); §3.1 equations (1)–(4) (split R-hat); §3.2 equations (10)–(13) (multi-chain ESS and positive/monotone paired sequence); §§4.1–4.4 equations (14)–(20) (rank normalization, folding, bulk/tail ESS, quantile indicators and Beta-quantile MCSE); §§5.1–5.2 (Cauchy and centered eight-schools simulations).

contents.name: Split R-hat variance formula and chain-splitting rationale, §3.1 — alg-split-rhat-from-multiple-chains
contents.reason: The local procedures specify equal splitting, the W/B/V+ formulas, the odd-length convention, and the undefined W=0 boundary.

contents.name: Split R-hat variance formula and chain-splitting rationale, §3.1 — alg-rank-normalized-folded-split-rhat

contents.name: Blom average-rank normal scores and folded deviations, §4.1–4.2, equation (14) — def-blom-rank-normalization-for-pooled-draws
contents.reason: The corrected v5 denominator S+1/4 is used. Average ranks for ties, pooled normalization, folding about the pooled median, and the maximum of rank and folded split-R-hat are stated locally.

contents.name: Combined multi-chain ESS and Geyer paired positive/monotone sequence, §3.2, equations (10)–(13) — def-functional-specific-effective-sample-size
contents.reason: The local definition separates the theoretical variance-equivalent ESS from the finite estimator. The algorithm includes between-chain adjustment, biased autocovariances, paired truncation, monotone truncation, and nonestimable boundaries.

contents.name: Combined multi-chain ESS and Geyer paired positive/monotone sequence, §3.2, equations (10)–(13) — alg-multichain-effective-sample-size
contents.reason: The finite estimator uses split chains, between/within adjustment, biased autocovariances, Geyer positive/monotone paired truncation, the source antithetic odd/even averaging convention and its short-chain software cap; it asserts no CLT or consistency.

contents.reason: The tail procedure uses ESS for the 5% and 95% quantile indicators; the quantile MCSE procedure uses the indicator at a requested empirical quantile.

contents.reason: The local algorithm states the Beta shapes, lower-quantile convention, empirical inverse-CDF mapping, and half-width approximation, while explicitly withholding a universal coverage guarantee.
